question: Every eval set caps a chapter at 300 characters and a draft at one to three sentences. What happens on a chapter the length real writing produces?
answer: It does not merely run long. It fails, returns nothing, and spends 78,878 tokens doing so.

environment.project: 灰港回声 seed work, Memory V4, 10 chapters
environment.note: A seed work was used because its Memory already exists; the draft is an 816-character chapter written for this test in that work's world, reusing its names so bounded retrieval would actually hit.

draft.splitter: re.split(r"(?<=[。！？])", draft_text) — one claim per sentence, v2_database.py
draft.planted_non_issue: 北潮闸未关而雾钟响 — chapter 10 already records this as an open thread, so reporting it would be a false positive

retrieval.note: Ten distinct spans occupied 113 evidence slots. This work's spans are about 35 characters each so the cost is small here; on a real chapter of a thousand characters the same duplication multiplies the input instead.

same_release_short_draft.note: Both issues correct, including one proved by combining a world-rule span with a fact span. No contract repair was needed.

comparison.dev_set_single_claim_drafts: median 14.6 s on the same release, one to three sentences each

findings.statement: A contract failure in one batch discards every other batch's finished work. 51,388 output tokens exceed the 16,000-token thinking cap of a single dispatch several times over, so the draft was split across batches and at least one of them completed; the run still returned zero issues.
findings.consequence: The chance that some claim trips a contract grows with claim count, so this failure mode arrives exactly when a chapter reaches realistic length.

findings.statement: The failure code is conflict_evidence_insufficient, raised when a possible_conflict or state_change issue cites a span whose sufficiency is insufficient (engine.py). The model answered that way, took its one bounded repair, answered the same way again, and the run failed closed.
findings.consequence: v22 deliberately steers undecidable tensions to possible_conflict, so this collision became common. Whether the guard itself is right for possible_conflict — an issue that by definition does not establish a contradiction — is worth re-examining, not only whether the review can be talked out of it.

findings.statement: One claim per sentence turns an ordinary 816-character chapter into 36 separately reasoned claims.
findings.consequence: Cost and failure probability both scale with sentence count rather than with how much of the chapter is actually checkable.

limits: One run. It is enough to act on because the outcome is a total failure on ordinary input, not a slow success.
